title: Shared function code basis with sparse private residuals
hypothesis: A shared signature/phase Mirror code plus sparse private residuals preserves off-orbit functions when exceptions are rare and is smaller than full per-function codes up to a measurable private-fraction boundary.
physical_object: one shared Fourier interpreter with four phase-view signatures
mirror_coordinate: one Givens phase per function; sparse private residual coefficients for off-orbit frequency-5 behavior
logical_multiplicity: 64 functions, each either on the shared phase orbit or carrying a private residual
controls: shared Mirror signatures/angles with no private residual
partial private residual recovery at 0%, 50%, and 100% of private functions
fixture: 64 functions; base sin(omega_s*x+phase) over four signatures; private tasks add 0.35*sin(5*x+psi); sweep private fractions 0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1

development.selection_metric: mean function NRMSE2 and actual serialized payload bytes across private fractions/residual counts

paid_objects: all signature IDs and Mirror angles
every private residual index and value

compute.proxy: report shared phase decode plus active residual additions; full code decodes ten Fourier coefficients per function

success_gate: At private fractions <=0.25, full residual recovery has NRMSE2 <=1e-6 and payload <=0.85x full per-function code; report the measured fraction where this stops holding.
failure_gate: No <=25% private point meets exact quality and byte ratio.
boundaries: Analytic Fourier function family, not a learned interpreter.
Private residuals are known deterministic target coefficients; no training or selection model.
No language or general task-capacity claim.
